title: Every Spell must carry an expiration date, capped at 90 days, and voters are told it explicitly
content:
A.1.10.2.4.8.2.4 requires that "the Spell must always have an expiration date; it can't be more than 90 days in the future, and the typical expiration window is 30 days." A.1.10.2.4.8.3.5 requires the voter-facing summary to say so in prescribed words: "If this Executive Proposal does not pass within 30 days, then it will expire and can no longer have any effect on the Sky Protocol."

An Executive Vote is therefore a time-limited grant of authority, not a permanent one. A Spell that passes but is never executed becomes inert, and re-authorization means going back to voters rather than reusing the old mandate.

The reasoning is the same as for StarGuard's `maxDelay` (A.1.10.2.3.2.3.1.1.2.4): an approved action carries the assumptions of the moment it was approved. Rates, balances, module states and other approved changes all move, and a mandate executed months later may do something quite different from what voters authorized in substance even while doing exactly what they authorized in text.

The pattern recurs at two layers — Spell expiry for Sky Core, `maxDelay` for whitelisted Agent Spells — which suggests a general principle rather than a local parameter: in this framework, authority decays by default and permanence must be argued for.

Requiring the expiry to be *stated to voters* completes it. The time limit is part of what is being voted on, so a holder can weigh whether the window is short enough for the risk the action carries.
description: A.1.10.2.4.8.2.4 makes a passed-but-unexecuted Spell die rather than persist; A.1.10.2.4.8.3.5 requires the expiry to be stated in the summary in fixed wording.
